description.value: The study examined how perceptual decision variables and confidence are represented and related in the human brain during a visual motion discrimination task using fMRI and multivariate decoding.

design.value: Nineteen young and neurologically healthy subjects performed a visual motion discrimination task during fMRI; one participant was subsequently excluded due to excessive head motion, leaving 18 subjects. Subjects made a binary perceptual judgment followed by a continuous confidence rating across five experimental runs of 72 trials each.

description.value: Subjects indicated their confidence by moving a white dot with a trackball to the part of a continuous confidence bar corresponding to their confidence. The scale ranged from “very sure about the direction of motion” to “no idea at all.”
Subjects judged the dominant direction of motion of the stimulus as “motion up” or “motion down.”

source_definition.value: The subject's binary perceptual choice, coded as -1 or 1 for “up” and “down,” respectively.
The direction of motion of the random dot motion stimulus, either upward or downward.
The continuous confidence ratings were divided into 3 confidence bins by separating each subject's ratings at the 33.3 and 66.6 percentiles: “low,” “medium,” and “high confidence.”

functional_form.value: linear increase or decrease across different confidence levels

source_definition.value: A proxy of the decision variable was constructed on each trial by multiplying the binary choice, coded as -1 or 1 for “up” and “down,” respectively, with the binned confidence rating, coded as 0.5, 1.5, and 2.5 for equidistant labels.

functional_form.value: product of binary choice and binned confidence rating

source_definition.value: Response time was included as the first parametric regressor in a repeated mass-univariate analysis, with confidence as the second parametric regressor.

description.value: Nineteen young and neurologically healthy subjects took part in the study; one participant was subsequently excluded due to excessive head motion, leaving 18 subjects.

consented_count.value: All 19 subjects provided informed consent for participation.

enrolled_count.value: Nineteen subjects took part in the study.

task_description.value: Subjects observed a random dot motion stimulus with an individually calibrated percentage of dots moving either upward or downward while all other dots moved in random directions. They made two consecutive responses: a binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion and a rating of confidence on a continuous scale.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to respond even when they were very unsure. For the confidence judgment, they were instructed that the scale ranged from “very sure about the direction of motion” to “no idea at all,” and that the center indicated the border between rather sure and rather unsure.

stimuli.value: A random dot motion stimulus was presented for 1 s. It contained 500 dots in a 10 × 10 dva square region, visible within a circular annulus with outer radius 5 dva and inner radius 0.85 dva. Signal dots moved upward or downward at 2.5 dva/s, while noise dots moved in equally spaced directions.

task_description.value: After the main experiment, all subjects took part in a functional localizer run to locate motion-sensitive region MT+/V5 in each individual subject.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla TIM Trio MRI (Siemens) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: T2*-weighted gradient-echo echo-planar images were acquired with 33 descending slices. In total, 2247 functional volumes were acquired per subject, corresponding to the experimental runs and the functional localizer. The first 2 functional volumes were automatically discarded in each run to allow for T1 equilibrium effects.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla TIM Trio MRI (Siemens) with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: A T1-weighted MPRAGE volume was acquired for inter-subject normalization and mapping functional images to reference structural images.
In all three analyses, functional images were first spatially realigned and slice-timing corrected.
For the univariate analysis, the functional images were spatially normalized using the transformation matrix derived from the structural images and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: spatial normalization using the transformation matrix
smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM

description.value: For both multivariate analyses, functional data were not spatially warped or smoothed.

Using the structural images of all subjects, a template structural reference image was created using DARTEL. For comparability with other studies, this template was brought to MNI space using affine transformation, and the transformation matrices of each subject were saved.

steps.value: creation of a template structural reference image using DARTEL
affine transformation of the template to MNI space
saving of each subject's transformation matrices

model_settings.value: A GLM with 10 regressors per run modeled a 2-s boxcar stimulation regressor, a parametric modulator reflecting the linear increase or decrease in BOLD signal across the three confidence levels, missed trials, six head-motion regressors, and a constant term. A 1/128-Hz high-pass filter was applied.

level.value: first-level subject analysis followed by group-level t-tests

estimator.value: SPM8 GLM estimation; resulting contrast images were submitted to group-level t-tests

model_settings.value: The same mass-univariate analysis was repeated using response time as the first and confidence as the second parametric regressor. Confidence was orthogonalized with respect to response time.

level.value: first-level subject analysis followed by group-level analysis

estimator.value: SPM8 GLM estimation with confidence orthogonalized with respect to response time

model_settings.value: Choices were modeled separately for both directions of motion: “motion up, choice up,” “motion up, choice down,” “motion down, choice up,” and “motion down, choice down.” Missed trials, movement in six regressors, and a baseline regressor were also modeled, leading to 12 regressors per run.

level.value: first-level subject analysis followed by group-level t-test

model_settings.value: The three decision variables were modeled separately for the two choices, resulting in six regressors per run. Missed trials, motion regressors, and a baseline regressor were added.

level.value: first-level subject analysis followed by group-level analysis

model_settings.value: A searchlight sphere with a radius of 10 mm containing 139 voxels was used. Parameter estimates for the two choice regressors for each of five runs were classified with a linear support vector machine using a leave-one-run-out cross-validation scheme. The standard cost value was c = 1; group-level inference tested whether accuracy exceeded 50%.

level.value: within-subject searchlight analysis followed by group-level t-test

model_settings.value: A searchlight sphere with a radius of 10 mm was used. Six parameter-estimate patterns per run were assigned labels ranging from -2.5 to 2.5. A linear nu-SVR was used with nu = 0.5 and c = 1, and the model was trained and tested with leave-one-run-out cross-validation.

level.value: within-subject searchlight analysis followed by group-level t-test

estimator.value: Fisher-z-transformed correlation between true and predicted labels, averaged across runs

model_settings.value: Predicted decision-variable labels from 12 candidate seed regions were transformed into predicted confidence values and correlated with predicted confidence values in the ventral striatum across runs. Regions were defined by 10-mm spheres around subject-specific peaks. A permutation test used 120 possible run combinations per subject and was repeated 10^6 times; significance used Bonferroni correction across 12 regions.

estimator.value: Fisher-z-transformed across-run correlations and permutation testing

name.value: Negative parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: A negative linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs.

model_representation_notes.value: The GLM included a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter, six head-motion regressors, and a constant term.

interpretations.value: Many of the regions displaying a negative relationship with confidence no longer survived the statistical threshold after response-time variance was removed; at a more lenient threshold, these effects were strongly reduced by the inclusion of response time.

role.value: included independent of the direction of motion

definition.value: The binary choice, coded as -1 or 1 for “up” and “down,” respectively, multiplied with the binned confidence rating, coded as 0.5, 1.5, and 2.5.

specific_metric.value: correlation between the true labels and the labels predicted from the regression model

structured_details.value: {"searchlight_radius":"10 mm","regression_model":"linear support vector regression (nu-SVR)","parameters":"nu = 0.5; cost value c = 1","validation":"leave-one-run-out cross-validation"}

reason_first_class_type_not_used.value: The analysis used multivariate support vector regression rather than classification, representational similarity, connectivity, conjunction, or component decomposition.

model_representation_notes.value: The parameter estimates of the GLM reflecting the decision variable were used as inputs to the multivariate regression analysis; labels ranged from -2.5 to 2.5.

interpretations.value: Activity patterns in a number of predominantly frontal and parietal brain regions were consistent with a representation of the decision variable.

name.value: positive parametric effect related to confidence

definition.value: A positive linear relationship between the BOLD signal amplitude and the confidence of the subject across all experimental runs.

model_representation_notes.value: The GLM included a 1/128-Hz high-pass filter, six head-motion regressors, and a constant term.

interpretations.value: The ventral striatum around the nucleus accumbens exhibited a robust positive correlation with confidence and was the primary candidate region for encoding perceptual confidence.

title.value: Brain regions where activity is related to confidence

footer.value: A complete list of brain regions with parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence. The coordinates and z-values refer to the peak within each cluster. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: The table reports brain regions with parametric increases and decreases in brain activity in relationship to confidence.

title.value: Brain regions informative about the DV

footer.value: Brain regions carrying information about the DV reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings. Mean Fisher z-values reflect the z-transformed size of the correlation between predicted and true values in the multivariate regression analysis, averaged across subjects. The coordinates, mean Fisher z-values, and statistical z-values of the normal distribution refer to the peak within each cluster. For clusters spanning several brain regions, multiple peaks are shown. Results are reported at P < 0.0001, corrected family-wise for cluster size at P < 0.05.

description.value: The table reports brain regions carrying information about the decision variable reconstructed from choices and confidence ratings.
